paper.title: Spectral Entry-wise Matrix Estimation for Low-Rank Reinforcement Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Low-rank bandit (regret minimization), homogeneous reward matrix
unmapped: Arms are entries (i,j) of an m x n reward matrix M of rank r
Reward matrix assumed homogeneous: m=Theta(n), kappa, mu, ||M||_inf, r all Theta(1)
Noise zero-mean and bounded: |xi_t| <= c1 ||M||_inf a.s.
Algorithm constant depends on upper bounds on incoherence mu, condition number kappa and ||M||_inf; rank r used for spectral estimation
settings.definition_quote: Consider a low-rank bandit problem with a homogeneous rank-$r$ reward matrix $M$. ... The regret up to round $T$ is defined by $R^\pi(T)=T M_{i^\star,j^\star} - \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^TM_{i_t^\pi,j_t^\pi}]$

settings.name_in_paper: Best entry identification in low-rank bandits
unmapped: Arms are entries of an m x n homogeneous rank-r reward matrix
Algorithm constant depends on upper bounds on mu, kappa, ||M||_inf
settings.definition_quote: SME-AE (Successive Matrix Estimation and Arm Elimination), an algorithm meant to identify the best entry as quickly as possible with a prescribed level of certainty.

settings.name_in_paper: Reward-free RL in low-rank MDPs (forward model)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Discounted MDP reward-free RL, not a bandit problem
unmapped: n states, A actions, rank-r transition matrices, discount gamma
settings.definition_quote: A low-rank MDP is defined by $(\SSS,\AAA,\{P^{a}\}_{a\in\AAA},R,\gamma)$ ... In the reward-free RL setting, the learner does not receive any reward signal during the exploration process.

algorithms.name: SME-AE (Successive Matrix Estimation and Arm Elimination)
Spectral model estimation + planning (reward-free low-rank MDP)

symbols.m_rows: number of rows of the reward matrix
symbols.n_cols: number of columns of the reward matrix

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: (Best entry identification) For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, SME-AE($\delta$) stops at time $\tau$ and recommends arm $(\hat{\imath}_\tau, \hat{\jmath}_\tau)$ with the guarantee $\PP \big( (\hat{\imath}_\tau, \hat{\jmath}_\tau) = (i^\star,j^\star),  \tau \le   \psi(n,m,\delta) \big)  \ge  1-\delta$.

results.notes: Correct identification and stopping time bound hold jointly with probability >= 1-delta. Homogeneity is assumed at the start of Section 4.

symbols.alpha_conf: exponent alpha>0 such that delta = T^{-alpha}

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Moreover, for any $T \ge 1$ and $\alpha>0$, the sample complexity $\tau$ of SME-AE($1/T^\alpha$) satisfies $\EE[\tau \wedge T] \le \psi(n,m,T^{-\alpha}) + T^{1-\alpha}$.

symbols.Delta_bar: average gap over all mn entries

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: (Regret) Let $T \ge 1$. Consider the algorithm $\pi$ that first runs SME-AE($1/T^2$) and then commits to its output $(\hat{\imath}_\tau, \hat{\jmath}_\tau)$ after $\tau$. We have: $R^\pi(T) \le  \bar{\Delta}\left( \psi(n,m,T^{-2})+ 1 \right) + \frac{\Delta_{\max}}{T}$.

results.notes: Scales as O((m+n) log^3(T) Delta_bar / Delta_min^2). The appendix also derives, informally (not as a formal statement), a gap-independent bound O~(zeta sqrt((n+m)T) log^2((n+m)T)) with zeta = Delta_max/Delta_min.

conditions: M^a homogeneous for all actions a

source.label: lemma:V_bound_MDP_forward
source.quote: Assume that for any $a\in {\cal A}$, $M^a$ is homogeneous ... If $T\ge c nA\log^2(nAT)$ ... then we have with probability at least $1-\min\{n^{-2},T^{-1}\}$: $\Gamma=\sup_R \| V^{\pi^\star(R)}_R - V^{\hat{\pi}(R)}_{R} \|_{\infty} \lesssim \frac{1}{(1-\gamma)^2}  \sqrt{\frac{nA}{T}} \log(nAT)$.

results.notes: Value suboptimality uniformly over reward functions; failure probability is min(n^-2, T^-1). Out-of-scope RL result.
